name: Treasure Data
description: Treasure Data is a customer data platform for collecting, unifying, governing, analyzing, and activating customer data across marketing and business systems. Its platform includes databases, data workbench, audience segmentation, workflows, connectors, identity resolution, profiles, analytics, and regional REST APIs.
agentUseSummary: Add a dedicated restricted-user Treasure Data API key and bind one exact US, Tokyo, AP02, or EU01 region; agents can read only database and delete-protected counts.

credentialRequirements.name: TREASURE_DATA_API_KEY
credentialRequirements.label: Treasure Data API key
credentialRequirements.helpText: Use a separate Master-type key owned by a dedicated restricted user whose permissions expose only the databases needed for this inventory count. Relay encrypts and never returns it.

credentialRequirements.name: TREASURE_DATA_API_REGION
credentialRequirements.label: Treasure Data API region
credentialRequirements.helpText: Bind exactly one official TD API region: us, tokyo, ap02, or eu01.

capabilities.label: Read database readiness summary
capabilities.description: Aggregate database and delete-protected counts while excluding database identity, record counts, permission details, tables, schemas, queries, jobs, and customer data.

approvalRequired.label: Get Treasure Data database readiness summary
approvalRequired.description: Return only database and delete-protected counts from the fixed regional database-list endpoint.

blocked.label: Access database identity, records, or permissions
blocked.description: Database IDs, names, organizations, record counts, permission fields, owners, timestamps, and individual database detail remain blocked.

blocked.label: Access tables, schemas, profiles, or customer data
blocked.description: Tables, columns, schemas, rows, profiles, identities, events, audiences, segments, attributes, behaviors, PII, consent, and raw customer data remain blocked.

blocked.label: Access queries, jobs, workflows, or integrations
blocked.description: SQL, query results, jobs, schedules, workflows, connectors, authentications, sources, destinations, imports, exports, activations, and delivery state remain blocked.

blocked.label: Create, update, delete, or administer Treasure Data
blocked.description: Database/table/data mutations, query execution, ingestion, activation, users, policies, API keys, settings, audit access, and administration remain blocked.

blocked.label: Use raw API or bulk access
blocked.description: Arbitrary regions, origins, paths, methods, headers, queries, bodies, filters, pagination, polling, retries, SDKs, CLI, browser sessions, bulk, and exports remain blocked.

approvalProfiles.label: Safe
approvalProfiles.description: The bounded database readiness read requires approval; identity, records, customer data, queries, jobs, imports, exports, writes, administration, raw APIs, and bulk remain blocked.

approvalProfiles.label: Dangerously skip permissions
approvalProfiles.description: The same bounded read runs directly; restricted-user authority, region binding, redaction, response cap, audits, and provider limits remain mandatory.

runtimeSupport.description: OpenClaw receives one fixed regional identity-free Treasure Data database-readiness wrapper.
Hermes receives the same fixed Treasure Data wrapper.

providerSetup.blocker: Treasure Data read APIs require a Master-type key, which inherits every permission of its owner; safe use requires a dedicated restricted user, narrowly assigned database permissions, exact region, IP allowlist compatibility, and live acceptance.
providerSetup.nextAction: A customer administrator creates a dedicated restricted user, assigns only necessary database visibility, creates a separate Master-type key, confirms the exact region and any IP allowlist, and completes a live read-only acceptance check.

evidence.supports: Treasure Data documents TD API authentication using Authorization: TD1 and the List Databases example as a core read operation.

The official TD API v3 OpenAPI documents four servers, GET /database/list with require_permissions, TD1 ApiKeyAuth, and a rich database response containing counts and identity fields that Relay excludes.

Treasure Data documents Master and write-only keys, warns that Master keys can read and write according to all user permissions, recommends separate keys and secure server-side storage, and supports revocation.
Treasure Data documents restricted-user database access through granular policy-based Full, Limited, Query-only, Import-only, General, Download, and Manage Own permissions.

securityNotes: Relay encrypts the customer-owned key and exact region binding; the key is sent only in the TD1 Authorization header to one allowlisted official TD API origin.
Relay accepts only us, tokyo, ap02, or eu01 and maps those identifiers to fixed provider origins; agents cannot supply regions, hosts, paths, or query parameters.
Relay allowlists only GET /v3/database/list?require_permissions=true, rejects redirects, waits 30 seconds, caps the response at 1 MB, and never paginates or retries automatically.
Output contains only database and delete-protected counts; database identity, record counts, permission details, tables, schemas, queries, jobs, profiles, and customer data are excluded.
Because a Master key inherits all owner permissions, Relay requires a dedicated restricted user and narrowly assigned database access even though the wrapper itself is read-only.
User/key creation, permission assignment, region and IP allowlist confirmation, key capture, rotation/revocation planning, and live acceptance remain customer/external steps.
